earnings.title: Marathon Petroleum Corp. Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results
highlights: Third-quarter net income attributable to MPC of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 per diluted share, adjusted net income of $7.5 billion, or $26.93 per diluted share
(NYSE: MPC) today reported net income attributable to MPC of $7.4 billion, or $26.59 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 .
This compares with a net income attributable to MPC of $1.4 billion, or $4.51 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.
Adjusted net income was $7.5 billion, or $26.93 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026.
This compares to adjusted net income of $915 million, or $3.01 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.

quotes.text: Our value chain capabilities remain a defining advantage for us, capturing opportunities to enhance margins across dynamic market conditions.
quotes.by: Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer Maryann Mannen

outlook: MPLX will receive $750 million of the proceeds, representing a 9x multiple on forecast 2027 adjusted EBITDA of the associated logistics assets.
MPC’s 2026 capital spending outlook (excluding MPLX) is $1.5 billion.

items.heading: Our financial results are affected by volatile refining margins, which are dependent on factors beyond our control.
Industry, market, technological and regulatory developments regarding emissions, fuel efficiency and alternative fuel vehicles may decrease demand for liquid transportation fuels.
Our operations are subject to business interruptions and present inherent hazards and risks, which could adversely impact our results of operations and financial condition.
We are increasingly dependent on the performance of our information technology systems and those of our third-party business partners and service providers.

Increasing regulatory focus on and expanding laws related to data privacy issues could expose us to increased liability, subject us to lawsuits, investigations, reputational harm and increase costs and restrictions on our operations that could significantly and adversely affect our business.
As we integrate artificial intelligence technologies into our processes, these technologies may present business, compliance and reputational risks.
